renders._yaml:
- component: card
  id: clusters_by_status
  title: Contig clusters
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of contig clusters, and the bar splits them into those a consensus was refined from and those that were filtered out. It answers how many clusters turned into genomes.
    How to read: clusters filtered out are usually small groups of contigs holding few reads, which the pipeline treats as likely false positives. A sample with every cluster filtered out produced no de novo genome.
    Lines and annotations: a cluster is filtered out when the contigs in it hold less than 5 percent of the mapped reads by default (perc_reads_contig), or when it is a singleton and singleton filtering is on.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/viralmetagenome/blob/1.2.0/nextflow_schema.json
  column: member_bp
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: status
  caption: clusters, by status

- component: card
  title: Read depth by cluster type
  description: |-
    The hero number is the summed share of contig read depth held by all clusters, and the bars rank the cluster types, reference-anchored or contig-only. It answers whether the reads sit in clusters anchored on a reference sequence.
    How to read: a high share in reference-anchored clusters means the sample's contigs match known viruses. A high share in contig-only clusters points to sequence with no close reference, or to contamination.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/viralmetagenome/blob/1.2.0/docs/output.md
  column: read_depth_pct
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: cluster_type
  top_n_count: 2
  caption: depth share, by cluster type

- component: figure
  title: Read depth share per cluster
  description: |-
    Each bar is a sample and its segments are its contig clusters, sized by the share of the sample's contig read depth they hold and coloured by status. It answers how the reads of each sample divide among clusters.
    How to read: one large refined segment is a clean single-virus sample. Many segments or a large filtered-out segment mean mixed or fragmented assembly, so check the contigs and their taxonomic calls.
    Lines and annotations: none are drawn. The pipeline's own cut-off is 5 percent of mapped reads per cluster (perc_reads_contig), a run parameter.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/viralmetagenome/blob/1.2.0/nextflow_schema.json
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: read_depth_pct
    color: status
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      read_depth_pct: Share of contig read depth (%)
      status: Cluster status

- component: table
  title: Contig clusters table
  description: |-
    Each row is a contig cluster with its taxon, centroid, member contigs, summed length, read depth share and status. It answers what each cluster holds and whether it became a consensus, and lets a row selection filter the other tiles.
    How to read: sort by read depth share to find the dominant clusters, and read the status to see which were discarded.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: sample

- component: card
  title: Contig taxonomic calls
  description: |-
    Each unit is one contig and the ring splits them into classified and unclassified by the merged Kraken2 and Kaiju call. It answers how much of the assembly the classifiers could place in a taxon.
    How to read: a ring mostly classified means the contigs resemble known viruses. A large unclassified share points to novel sequence, chimeric contigs or classifier databases that lack the virus.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/viralmetagenome/blob/1.2.0/docs/output.md
  column: contig
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: classification
  caption: contigs, classified or not

- component: table
  title: Contig classification table
  description: |-
    Each row is a contig, or a reference-pool sequence clustered with them, with its merged classification and taxon id. It answers how each contig was called before clustering.
    How to read: filter to unclassified contigs to see the sequence the classifiers could not place.

outputs.name: De novo consensus across refinement steps

renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: ambiguous_by_step
  title: Ambiguous bases across refinement
  description: |-
    Each line is a de novo consensus genome: its share of ambiguous bases at every step, from the scaffold built from contigs through each mapping iteration to the final variant-calling round. It answers whether refinement fills or creates gaps.
    How to read: a flat low line means refinement left the genome unambiguous. A line that rises means positions were masked as the reads were mapped, which happens where depth is too low to call a base.
    Lines and annotations: none are drawn. Positions covered by fewer than 5 reads are masked in the consensus by default (min_consensus_depth).
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/viralmetagenome/blob/1.2.0/nextflow_schema.json
  kind: profile
  config:
    x_title: Refinement step (0 is the scaffold)
    y_title: Ambiguous bases (%)
  roles:
    series: genome_id
    x: step_order
    y: n_pct

- component: advanced_viz
  id: identity_by_step
  title: Identity to the closest reference across refinement
  description: |-
    Each line is a de novo consensus genome: its identity to the closest sequence of the annotation database at every refinement step. It answers how far refinement moved the consensus away from the scaffold and from that reference.
    How to read: a flat line means refinement changed little. Identity falling across steps is expected when the sample differs from the reference, since the consensus follows the reads. A line low from the start is a divergent virus or a poor assembly.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/viralmetagenome/blob/1.2.0/docs/output.md
  kind: profile
  config:
    x_title: Refinement step (0 is the scaffold)
    y_title: Identity to the closest reference (%)
  roles:
    series: genome_id
    x: step_order
    y: annotation_identity_pct

- component: card
  title: Mismatches to the closest reference
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of mismatches between the final consensus and its closest annotated reference, and the box shows their quartiles. It answers how far the finished genomes sit from known sequence.
    How to read: few mismatches mean a genome close to a known virus. Many mismatches point to a divergent virus or an unreliable consensus, so check the ambiguous bases and the depth.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/viralmetagenome/blob/1.2.0/docs/output.md
  column: annotation_mismatches
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  filter_expr: col('step') == 'itvariant-calling'
  caption: mismatches, with their spread

- component: table
  title: Refinement steps table
  description: |-
    Each row is a consensus genome at one refinement step, with its length, ambiguous bases, identity and mismatches to the closest reference, depth and CheckV call. It answers how each metric changed between steps and lets a row selection filter the other tiles.
    How to read: sort by genome and step to follow one genome through the refinement.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: genome_id

- component: card
  id: contigs_by_class
  title: De novo contigs
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of de novo contigs, and the bar splits them by the merged Kraken2 and Kaiju call. It answers how many contigs were assembled and how many could be placed in a taxon.
    How to read: a large classified share means the assembly resembles known viruses. A large unclassified share points to novel sequence, chimeric contigs or a classifier database without the virus.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/viralmetagenome/blob/1.2.0/docs/output.md
  column: length_bp
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: classification
  caption: contigs, classified or not
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: assembled_bp
  title: Assembled length
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total number of assembled bases, and the bar splits it by contig length band. It answers how much of the assembly sits in long, usable contigs.
    How to read: most bases in long bands mean a contiguous assembly. Bases in short bands are fragments that the clustering may discard.
    Lines and annotations: contigs shorter than 500 bases are dropped by default (min_contig_size), so none appear in the shortest band.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/viralmetagenome/blob/1.2.0/nextflow_schema.json
  column: length_bp
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: length_class
  caption: bases, by contig length band

- component: card
  id: reads_on_contigs
  title: Reads on contigs
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of reads that map back to the contigs, and the ring splits them by the role of their contig in its cluster: centroid or member. It answers where the sequencing effort went.
    How to read: reads concentrated on centroids and members of refined clusters are well used. Reads on contigs that never clustered were not carried into a consensus.
  column: mapped_reads
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: cluster_role
  caption: reads, by cluster role

- component: advanced_viz
  id: length_vs_reads
  title: Contig length against mapped reads
  description: |-
    Each point is a de novo contig: its length on the horizontal axis and the reads that map back to it on the vertical axis, sized by its share of the sample's reads and coloured by its taxonomic call. It answers whether long contigs are supported by the reads.
    How to read: long contigs with many reads are well supported. A long contig with few reads may be a chimera or a contaminant, and a short contig with many reads is a fragment of a deeply covered genome. Both axes are logarithmic.
    Lines and annotations: none are drawn, because the pipeline publishes no length-to-reads cut-off.
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Contig length (bp)
    y_title: Reads mapped to the contig
    log_x: true
    log_y: true
    top_n_labels: 5
  roles:
    x: length_bp
    y: mapped_reads
    label: contig
    color: classification
    size: read_share_pct

- component: interactive
  title: Taxonomic call
  description: Keeps only contigs with the chosen call, classified or unclassified.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: classification

- component: table
  title: De novo contigs table
  description: |-
    Each row is a de novo contig with its assembler, length, mapped reads, read share, taxonomic call and cluster. It answers how each contig was built and where it ended up, and lets a row selection filter the other tiles.
    How to read: sort by mapped reads to see the best supported contigs, and by length to see the longest.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: sample

- component: card
  id: denovo_genomes
  title: De novo consensus genomes
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of final de novo consensus genomes, and the bar splits them by the virus of their closest annotated reference. It answers what the run reconstructed.
    How to read: genomes of the expected virus are the result, and other viruses may be co-infections or contamination. Genomes with no assigned virus had no significant hit in the annotation database.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/viralmetagenome/blob/1.2.0/docs/output.md
  column: genome_id
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: virus
  caption: genomes, by virus
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: denovo_ambiguous
  title: Ambiguous bases per genome
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of ambiguous bases (N) in the final consensus genomes, and the box shows their quartiles. It answers how complete the called sequence is.
    How to read: a median near zero means the genomes are fully called. A high median or a long upper whisker marks genomes with gaps, usually where depth was too low to call a base.
    Lines and annotations: none are drawn. The pipeline masks positions covered by fewer than 5 reads by default (min_consensus_depth) and publishes no cut-off for the share of ambiguous bases of a genome.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/viralmetagenome/blob/1.2.0/nextflow_schema.json
  column: n_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: ambiguous bases (%), with their spread

- component: advanced_viz
  id: denovo_identity_vs_n
  title: Ambiguous bases against identity
  description: |-
    Each point is a final de novo consensus genome: its share of ambiguous bases on the horizontal axis and its identity to the closest annotated reference on the vertical axis, sized by mean depth and coloured by virus. It answers which genomes are both complete and close to a known sequence.
    How to read: genomes at the top left are fully called and close to a reference. Genomes to the right have gaps, and those low on the axis are divergent or poorly assembled, so check their depth before using them.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median identity to the closest reference of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of the pipeline or the annotation database.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/viralmetagenome/blob/1.2.0/docs/output.md
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Ambiguous bases (%)
    y_title: Identity to the closest reference (%)
    top_n_labels: 5
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
  roles:
    x: n_pct
    y: annotation_identity_pct
    label: genome_id
    color: virus
    size: mean_depth

- component: table
  title: De novo genomes table
  description: |-
    Each row is a final de novo consensus genome with its closest reference, identity, ambiguous bases, best BLAST hit, CheckV call, mapping, depth and variant counts. It answers how good each reconstructed genome is, and lets a row selection filter the other tiles.
    How to read: sort by ambiguous bases or identity, and read the CheckV call and the depth before accepting a genome.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: genome_id

outputs.name: Consensus genomes against the mapping constraints

renders._yaml:
- component: card
  id: constraint_breadth
  title: Breadth at 10x depth
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of the constraint genome covered by at least 10 reads, and the histogram shows it for every sample and reference. It answers how completely the reads cover each reference.
    How to read: values near 100 mean a fully covered genome. A low tail marks references the sample barely contains, and their consensus is mostly masked.
    Lines and annotations: none are drawn. The pipeline masks positions covered by fewer than 5 reads by default (min_consensus_depth) and publishes no breadth cut-off.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/viralmetagenome/blob/1.2.0/nextflow_schema.json
  column: cov_10x_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: genome covered at 10x (%), per genome
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: constraint_depth
  title: Mean depth
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median of the mean read depth over the constraint genomes, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how deeply the reads cover the references.
    How to read: higher depth supports a confident consensus. A low box means many positions fall under the minimum depth and are masked.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/viralmetagenome/blob/1.2.0/nextflow_schema.json
  column: mean_depth
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: mean depth, with its spread

- component: advanced_viz
  id: depth_vs_breadth
  title: Depth against breadth
  description: |-
    Each point is a sample mapped to one constraint reference: its mean depth on the horizontal axis and the share of the genome covered at 10x or more on the vertical axis, sized by mapped reads and coloured by reference. It answers whether a deep mapping is also a complete one.
    How to read: points at the top right are deep and complete. A deep but narrow mapping is a partial genome, and a broad but shallow one is masked in places, so look at the other references of the same sample.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median share of the genome covered at 10x of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of the pipeline.
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Mean depth
    y_title: Genome covered at 10x (%)
    top_n_labels: 5
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
  roles:
    x: mean_depth
    y: cov_10x_pct
    label: genome_id
    color: reference
    size: mapped_reads

- component: table
  title: Constraint mappings table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample mapped to a constraint reference, with its consensus, closest annotated reference, ambiguous bases, CheckV call, reads mapped and duplicated, depth, breadth and variant counts. It answers how each mapping performed and lets a row selection filter the other tiles.
    How to read: sort by breadth or ambiguous bases, and compare the references of one sample to see which one fits its reads.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: genome_id

outputs.name: Reads, host removal and assembly per sample

renders._yaml:
- component: card
  id: read_attrition
  title: Read pairs through preprocessing
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of raw read pairs, and the bars show how many remain after trimming and after host removal. It answers how much sequencing reaches the assembly.
    How to read: a small loss at each step is normal. A large loss at trimming means poor read quality or adapters, and a large loss at host removal means a host-rich sample.
  column: raw_read_pairs
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: attrition
  attrition_cols:
  - trimmed_read_pairs
  - host_filtered_read_pairs
  caption: read pairs, at each step
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: retained_share
  title: Reads retained
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of raw read pairs left after preprocessing, and the box shows the quartiles over samples. It answers how much of each library survives.
    How to read: values near 100 are libraries with little loss. A long lower whisker marks samples that lost many reads and may be too shallow to assemble.
  column: retained_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: reads retained (%), with their spread

- component: card
  id: host_share
  title: Host reads
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of reads removed as host, and the histogram shows it for every sample. It answers how host-rich the samples are.
    How to read: a high share means most sequencing went to the host, leaving less for the virus, and the highest samples are the ones to check first.
    Lines and annotations: none are drawn. Host removal uses a Kraken2 database and the pipeline publishes no cut-off for the host share.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/viralmetagenome/blob/1.2.0/docs/output.md
  column: host_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: host share (%), per sample

- component: card
  id: assembly_n50
  title: Assembly N50
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median N50 of the de novo assemblies, and the box shows the quartiles over samples. It answers how contiguous the assemblies are.
    How to read: for a virus with one genome segment, an N50 close to the genome length means a near-complete assembly. A low N50 means fragmented contigs that the clustering has to merge.
  column: assembly_n50
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: N50 (bp), with its spread

- component: advanced_viz
  id: retained_vs_host
  title: Reads retained against host share
  description: |-
    Each point is a sample: its share of host reads on the horizontal axis and the share of raw read pairs retained on the vertical axis, sized by raw read pairs. It answers why a sample lost reads.
    How to read: a sample low on both axes lost its reads to the host database. A sample low on retained reads with little host lost them at trimming, so check its quality and adapter content. Large points that stay high are well sequenced.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median share of read pairs retained of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of the pipeline.
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Host reads (%)
    y_title: Read pairs retained (%)
    top_n_labels: 5
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
  roles:
    x: host_pct
    y: retained_pct
    label: sample
    size: raw_read_pairs

- component: figure
  id: host_filtered_bars
  title: Read pairs after host removal
  description: |-
    Each bar is a sample: the read pairs left after host removal, coloured by the share of reads removed as host. It answers how much usable sequencing each sample has.
    How to read: short bars are samples with little left to assemble, and the colour says whether the host removal or a shallow library is the cause.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median number of read pairs after host removal of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of the pipeline.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: host_filtered_read_pairs
    color: host_pct
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      host_filtered_read_pairs: Read pairs after host removal
      host_pct: Host reads (%)
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: host_filtered_read_pairs

- component: interactive
  title: Host reads (%)
  description: Keeps only samples whose host share falls in the chosen range.
  interactive_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: host_pct

- component: table
  title: Samples overview table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample with its read pairs before and after trimming and host removal, its quality and duplication, the assembly length and N50, the clusters kept and removed and the de novo consensus count. It answers how every sample fared from reads to assembly and lets a row selection filter the other tiles.
    How to read: sort by retained share or host share to find the samples that lost the most reads, then read their assembly metrics.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: sample

- component: card
  id: clusters_by_status
  title: Contig clusters
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of contig clusters, and the bar splits them into those a consensus was refined from and those that were filtered out. It answers how many clusters turned into genomes.
    How to read: clusters filtered out are usually small groups of contigs holding few reads, which the pipeline treats as likely false positives. A sample with every cluster filtered out produced no de novo genome.
    Lines and annotations: a cluster is filtered out when the contigs in it hold less than 5 percent of the mapped reads by default (perc_reads_contig), or when it is a singleton and singleton filtering is on.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/viralmetagenome/blob/1.2.0/nextflow_schema.json
  column: member_bp
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:

  caption: clusters, by status

- component: card

    How to read: a high share in reference-anchored clusters means the sample's contigs match known viruses. A high share in contig-only clusters points to sequence with no close reference, or to contamination.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/viralmetagenome/blob/1.2.0/docs/output.md
  column: read_depth_pct
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: cluster_type
  top_n_count: 2
  caption: depth share, by cluster type

- component: figure
  title: Read depth share per cluster
  description: |-

    Lines and annotations: none are drawn. The pipeline's own cut-off is 5 percent of mapped reads per cluster (perc_reads_contig), a run parameter.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/viralmetagenome/blob/1.2.0/nextflow_schema.json
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: read_depth_pct
    color: status
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      read_depth_pct: Share of contig read depth (%)
      status: Cluster status

- component: table
  title: Contig clusters table
  description: |-
    Each row is a contig cluster with its taxon, centroid, member contigs, summed length, read depth share and status. It answers what each cluster holds and whether it became a consensus, and lets a row selection filter the other tiles.

- component: card

  column: contig

    The hero number is the median count of mismatches between the final consensus and its closest annotated reference, and the box shows their quartiles. It answers how far the finished genomes sit from known sequence.
    How to read: few mismatches mean a genome close to a known virus. Many mismatches point to a divergent virus or an unreliable consensus, so check the ambiguous bases and the depth.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/viralmetagenome/blob/1.2.0/docs/output.md
  column: annotation_mismatches
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  filter_expr: col('step') == 'itvariant-calling'
  caption: mismatches, with their spread

- component: table
  title: Refinement steps table
  description: |-
    Each row is a consensus genome at one refinement step, with its length, ambiguous bases, identity and mismatches to the closest reference, depth and CheckV call. It answers how each metric changed between steps and lets a row selection filter the other tiles.
    How to read: sort by genome and step to follow one genome through the refinement.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: genome_id

- component: card
  id: contigs_by_class
  title: De novo contigs
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of de novo contigs, and the bar splits them by the merged Kraken2 and Kaiju call. It answers how many contigs were assembled and how many could be placed in a taxon.
    How to read: a large classified share means the assembly resembles known viruses. A large unclassified share points to novel sequence, chimeric contigs or a classifier database without the virus.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/viralmetagenome/blob/1.2.0/docs/output.md
  column: length_bp
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: classification
  caption: contigs, classified or not
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: assembled_bp
  title: Assembled length
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total number of assembled bases, and the bar splits it by contig length band. It answers how much of the assembly sits in long, usable contigs.
    How to read: most bases in long bands mean a contiguous assembly. Bases in short bands are fragments that the clustering may discard.
    Lines and annotations: contigs shorter than 500 bases are dropped by default (min_contig_size), so none appear in the shortest band.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/viralmetagenome/blob/1.2.0/nextflow_schema.json
  column: length_bp
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: length_class
  caption: bases, by contig length band

- component: card
  id: reads_on_contigs
  title: Reads on contigs
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of reads that map back to the contigs, and the ring splits them by the role of their contig in its cluster: centroid or member. It answers where the sequencing effort went.
    How to read: reads concentrated on centroids and members of refined clusters are well used. Reads on contigs that never clustered were not carried into a consensus.
  column: mapped_reads
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: cluster_role
  caption: reads, by cluster role

- component: advanced_viz
  id: length_vs_reads
  title: Contig length against mapped reads
  description: |-
    Each point is a de novo contig: its length on the horizontal axis and the reads that map back to it on the vertical axis, sized by its share of the sample's reads and coloured by its taxonomic call. It answers whether long contigs are supported by the reads.
    How to read: long contigs with many reads are well supported. A long contig with few reads may be a chimera or a contaminant, and a short contig with many reads is a fragment of a deeply covered genome. Both axes are logarithmic.
    Lines and annotations: none are drawn, because the pipeline publishes no length-to-reads cut-off.
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Contig length (bp)
    y_title: Reads mapped to the contig
    log_x: true
    log_y: true
    top_n_labels: 5
  roles:
    x: length_bp
    y: mapped_reads
    label: contig
    color: classification
    size: read_share_pct

- component: interactive
  title: Taxonomic call
  description: Keeps only contigs with the chosen call, classified or unclassified.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: classification

- component: table
  title: De novo contigs table
  description: |-
    Each row is a de novo contig with its assembler, length, mapped reads, read share, taxonomic call and cluster. It answers how each contig was built and where it ended up, and lets a row selection filter the other tiles.
    How to read: sort by mapped reads to see the best supported contigs, and by length to see the longest.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: sample

- component: card
  id: denovo_genomes
  title: De novo consensus genomes
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of final de novo consensus genomes, and the bar splits them by the virus of their closest annotated reference. It answers what the run reconstructed.
    How to read: genomes of the expected virus are the result, and other viruses may be co-infections or contamination. Genomes with no assigned virus had no significant hit in the annotation database.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/viralmetagenome/blob/1.2.0/docs/output.md
  column: genome_id
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: virus
  caption: genomes, by virus
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: denovo_ambiguous
  title: Ambiguous bases per genome
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of ambiguous bases (N) in the final consensus genomes, and the box shows their quartiles. It answers how complete the called sequence is.
    How to read: a median near zero means the genomes are fully called. A high median or a long upper whisker marks genomes with gaps, usually where depth was too low to call a base.
    Lines and annotations: none are drawn. The pipeline masks positions covered by fewer than 5 reads by default (min_consensus_depth) and publishes no cut-off for the share of ambiguous bases of a genome.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/viralmetagenome/blob/1.2.0/nextflow_schema.json
  column: n_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: ambiguous bases (%), with their spread

- component: advanced_viz
  id: denovo_identity_vs_n
  title: Ambiguous bases against identity
  description: |-
    Each point is a final de novo consensus genome: its share of ambiguous bases on the horizontal axis and its identity to the closest annotated reference on the vertical axis, sized by mean depth and coloured by virus. It answers which genomes are both complete and close to a known sequence.
    How to read: genomes at the top left are fully called and close to a reference. Genomes to the right have gaps, and those low on the axis are divergent or poorly assembled, so check their depth before using them.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median identity to the closest reference of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of the pipeline or the annotation database.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/viralmetagenome/blob/1.2.0/docs/output.md
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Ambiguous bases (%)
    y_title: Identity to the closest reference (%)
    top_n_labels: 5
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
  roles:
    x: n_pct
    y: annotation_identity_pct
    label: genome_id
    color: virus
    size: mean_depth

- component: table
  title: De novo genomes table
  description: |-
    Each row is a final de novo consensus genome with its closest reference, identity, ambiguous bases, best BLAST hit, CheckV call, mapping, depth and variant counts. It answers how good each reconstructed genome is, and lets a row selection filter the other tiles.
    How to read: sort by ambiguous bases or identity, and read the CheckV call and the depth before accepting a genome.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: genome_id

outputs.name: Consensus genomes against the mapping constraints

renders._yaml:
- component: card
  id: constraint_breadth
  title: Breadth at 10x depth
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of the constraint genome covered by at least 10 reads, and the histogram shows it for every sample and reference. It answers how completely the reads cover each reference.
    How to read: values near 100 mean a fully covered genome. A low tail marks references the sample barely contains, and their consensus is mostly masked.
    Lines and annotations: none are drawn. The pipeline masks positions covered by fewer than 5 reads by default (min_consensus_depth) and publishes no breadth cut-off.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/viralmetagenome/blob/1.2.0/nextflow_schema.json
  column: cov_10x_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: genome covered at 10x (%), per genome
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: constraint_depth
  title: Mean depth
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median of the mean read depth over the constraint genomes, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how deeply the reads cover the references.
    How to read: higher depth supports a confident consensus. A low box means many positions fall under the minimum depth and are masked.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/viralmetagenome/blob/1.2.0/nextflow_schema.json
  column: mean_depth
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: mean depth, with its spread

- component: advanced_viz
  id: depth_vs_breadth
  title: Depth against breadth
  description: |-
    Each point is a sample mapped to one constraint reference: its mean depth on the horizontal axis and the share of the genome covered at 10x or more on the vertical axis, sized by mapped reads and coloured by reference. It answers whether a deep mapping is also a complete one.
    How to read: points at the top right are deep and complete. A deep but narrow mapping is a partial genome, and a broad but shallow one is masked in places, so look at the other references of the same sample.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median share of the genome covered at 10x of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of the pipeline.
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Mean depth
    y_title: Genome covered at 10x (%)
    top_n_labels: 5
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
  roles:
    x: mean_depth
    y: cov_10x_pct
    label: genome_id
    color: reference
    size: mapped_reads

- component: table
  title: Constraint mappings table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample mapped to a constraint reference, with its consensus, closest annotated reference, ambiguous bases, CheckV call, reads mapped and duplicated, depth, breadth and variant counts. It answers how each mapping performed and lets a row selection filter the other tiles.
    How to read: sort by breadth or ambiguous bases, and compare the references of one sample to see which one fits its reads.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: genome_id

outputs.name: Reads, host removal and assembly per sample

renders._yaml:
- component: card
  id: read_attrition
  title: Read pairs through preprocessing
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of raw read pairs, and the bars show how many remain after trimming and after host removal. It answers how much sequencing reaches the assembly.
    How to read: a small loss at each step is normal. A large loss at trimming means poor read quality or adapters, and a large loss at host removal means a host-rich sample.
  column: raw_read_pairs
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: attrition
  attrition_cols:
  - trimmed_read_pairs
  - host_filtered_read_pairs
  caption: read pairs, at each step
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: retained_share
  title: Reads retained
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of raw read pairs left after preprocessing, and the box shows the quartiles over samples. It answers how much of each library survives.
    How to read: values near 100 are libraries with little loss. A long lower whisker marks samples that lost many reads and may be too shallow to assemble.
  column: retained_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: reads retained (%), with their spread

- component: card
  id: host_share
  title: Host reads
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of reads removed as host, and the histogram shows it for every sample. It answers how host-rich the samples are.
    How to read: a high share means most sequencing went to the host, leaving less for the virus, and the highest samples are the ones to check first.
    Lines and annotations: none are drawn. Host removal uses a Kraken2 database and the pipeline publishes no cut-off for the host share.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/viralmetagenome/blob/1.2.0/docs/output.md
  column: host_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: host share (%), per sample

- component: card
  id: assembly_n50
  title: Assembly N50
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median N50 of the de novo assemblies, and the box shows the quartiles over samples. It answers how contiguous the assemblies are.
    How to read: for a virus with one genome segment, an N50 close to the genome length means a near-complete assembly. A low N50 means fragmented contigs that the clustering has to merge.
  column: assembly_n50
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: N50 (bp), with its spread

- component: advanced_viz
  id: retained_vs_host
  title: Reads retained against host share
  description: |-
    Each point is a sample: its share of host reads on the horizontal axis and the share of raw read pairs retained on the vertical axis, sized by raw read pairs. It answers why a sample lost reads.
    How to read: a sample low on both axes lost its reads to the host database. A sample low on retained reads with little host lost them at trimming, so check its quality and adapter content. Large points that stay high are well sequenced.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median share of read pairs retained of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of the pipeline.
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Host reads (%)
    y_title: Read pairs retained (%)
    top_n_labels: 5
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
  roles:
    x: host_pct
    y: retained_pct
    label: sample
    size: raw_read_pairs

- component: figure
  id: host_filtered_bars
  title: Read pairs after host removal
  description: |-
    Each bar is a sample: the read pairs left after host removal, coloured by the share of reads removed as host. It answers how much usable sequencing each sample has.
    How to read: short bars are samples with little left to assemble, and the colour says whether the host removal or a shallow library is the cause.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median number of read pairs after host removal of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of the pipeline.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: host_filtered_read_pairs
    color: host_pct
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      host_filtered_read_pairs: Read pairs after host removal
      host_pct: Host reads (%)
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: host_filtered_read_pairs

- component: interactive
  title: Host reads (%)
  description: Keeps only samples whose host share falls in the chosen range.
  interactive_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: host_pct

- component: table
  title: Samples overview table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample with its read pairs before and after trimming and host removal, its quality and duplication, the assembly length and N50, the clusters kept and removed and the de novo consensus count. It answers how every sample fared from reads to assembly and lets a row selection filter the other tiles.
    How to read: sort by retained share or host share to find the samples that lost the most reads, then read their assembly metrics.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: sample
